sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the tests
sections.what: Loads the built-in test and check tools, the reference slide builder, the citation function, the exporter, the pagination function and the result type.

sections.name: recipe (part 1)
sections.title: Sample result and first checks
sections.what: Builds a small sample result, then checks that every bullet, footnote and chart value on each slide has a matching citation entry, and that an unknown sentence is labelled as a gap. It also begins the splitting test on a long pillar slide.
sections.why: The test names say each finding keeps its own ID, so a slide claim cannot silently lose its source.
sections.watch_out: The sample has one project and two facts, so it cannot show problems that appear only with many projects.

sections.name: recipe: for
sections.title: Splitting, percentage and export checks
sections.what: Checks that split pillar pages keep each bullet's source, that conflicting saved cost percentages are flagged and left unchanged, and that the exported file has internal and external links, the expected text and the missing-source note.
sections.why: The three test names state the three concerns. The export test reads the saved file directly to confirm the links and notes are inside it.
sections.watch_out: The export test checks for certain words and link counts only, so it does not confirm how the slides look.

summary: Automated tests that check the source notes attached to slides, the splitting of long pillar slides, and the exported PowerPoint file.
purpose: Confirms that each bullet, footnote and chart value on a slide has a source record, that unknown claims show as gaps, and that the exported file has working links.
why: The test names state the rules they guard: provenance, alignment after splitting, no silent relabelling of percentages, and honest gaps.
how: Builds a small sample result with one project and two facts, builds the reference slides, and runs four tests. These check that citation counts match the slide content, that split pages keep the right source for each bullet, that conflicting cost percentages are flagged and kept, and that the exported file contains internal links, external links, the expected text and the missing-source note. The last test calls Python to read the saved file.
inputs: A hard-coded example result. No database is used.
outputs: A pass or fail for each test, with assertion messages when a check fails.
risks: The export test needs python3 on the machine. It uses a fixed example, so it does not cover real data.
debug: If the export test fails, confirm python3 is installed and run that test alone. If a splitting test fails, check the pagination function and the bullet number matching. If citation counts differ, compare the bullets and footnotes in the reference slide builder with the citation list.
